nodes.name: Sol-gel synthesis (Boudghene)
nodes.procedure: 0.02 mol of Na2WO4·2H2O and 0.02 mol of FeSO4·7H2O were dissolved in 20 cm³ of water, followed by the addition of 0.04 mol of citric acid powder. The resulting solution was stirred for 60 min at room temperature, leading to a translucent solution that formed a brownish gel when heated at 75°C for approximately 3 h. The gel was then dried at 100°C for 24 h, followed by calcination at 200°C for 6 h in air to eliminate impurities before storage for use as a catalyst.

nodes.name: Precipitation synthesis
nodes.procedure: Sodium tungstate was combined with ferric chloride in distilled water and stirred for 2 h, resulting in the formation of iron tungstate. The obtained product underwent washing, filtration, and drying at 100°C for an hour before being calcined at 500°C for 4 h in a muffle furnace, yielding brownish-black crystalline FeWO4 powder.

nodes.name: Microwave-hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Specific amounts of sodium tungstate (VI) dihydrate and sodium dodecyl sulfate in addition to ammonium iron (II) sulphate hexahydrate were dissolved in a solution maintained at pH 9 with NH4OH. Afterward, 100 cm³ of this mixture was transferred into a Teflon vessel autoclave and processed in a domestic microwave system at 443 K for 1 h, without agitation. Throughout the process, the temperature was monitored using an in-vessel sensor.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis with EDTA
nodes.procedure: Fe^{3+} and EDTA^{2-} created a stable complex, with Fe^{3+} being reduced to Fe^{2+} by formaldehyde. As hydrothermal conditions intensified over time and temperature, the Fe-EDTA complex weakened, allowing WO4^{2-} to replace EDTA^{2-}, forming FeWO4 nuclei. This led to a prolonged nucleation and growth process, enabling the formation of uniform crystals and hierarchical structures. Different concentrations of hexamethylenetetramine and chelating agents influenced the formation of FeWO4 crystals with varied shapes.
